aiSummary: Choctawhatchee Bay is fishing under full summer conditions today — sunny skies, a heat index hitting 103°F, and 87°F water mean an early start isn't optional, it's essential. Light west winds of 0–10 mph keep most water fishable through mid-morning, but a 12% storm chance after 1 PM is reason enough to be off the water or close to the ramp by early afternoon. The most recent bay-wide reports (late June) pointed to scattered but active speckled trout across the bay, quality bull redfish in backwater creeks off West Bay, and a strong recommendation for early morning trips — all of which still applies in spades today.

bridge.aiNote: The 331 Bridge spans the narrow neck of Choctawhatchee Bay, creating a current funnel where bait gets pushed through on both tides. Pilings hold trout, redfish, sheepshead, and black drum year-round, with the lee-side pilings serving as the prime ambush zone on incoming tides. Because it sits in open water, this spot is the first on the bay to become unfishable when wind picks up or chop builds.
bridge.todaysCall: High tide crested well before sunrise at 5:07 AM, so the tide will be falling through the morning — work the outgoing current against the pilings as bait flushes back into the bay. Light west winds of 0–10 mph should keep conditions manageable through mid-morning, so target the lee (east) side of the pilings early for trout and redfish before the sun climbs too high. Slightly stained water is a modest edge here since fish holding tight to structure won't be as easily spooked; darker soft plastics and noisy topwaters in the first hour of light can draw strikes. Wrap up well before 1 PM given the afternoon storm window — this exposed open-water spot offers no shelter if weather moves in.

alaqua.aiNote: Alaqua Bayou offers protected water with a strong year-round redfish population, plus trout and flounder at the creek mouth. The oyster bars at the mouth are the prime zone, and tree cover keeps the interior a few degrees cooler than the open bay while also providing shelter from wind and weather. The upper creek transitions toward brackish water and can hold bass alongside smaller reds.
alaqua.todaysCall: With the tide falling through the morning toward a 4:20 PM low, focus on the oyster bars at the creek mouth early — outgoing water will pull bait off the bars and stack reds and trout right at the edges. Tree cover is a real asset today given the brutal heat index, so push into the interior as the morning wears on and fish the shaded banks for reds. The new moon's spring-tide pull will give the outgoing some extra push, helping concentrate baitfish and predators alike at creek mouths and bar edges. Slightly stained water favors slower, more tactile presentations like a slow-rolled paddle tail on a light jig; finish well before the post-1 PM storm window.

basin.aiNote: Basin Bayou sees less fishing pressure than Alaqua and LaGrange, meaning the fish here tend to be less educated and more cooperative. The interior grass flats are classic sight-fishing territory for redfish in under two feet of water, and pompano occasionally appear at the mouth on moving tides in late spring and early summer. It is somewhat less protected than LaGrange when weather builds on the open bay.
basin.todaysCall: Light west winds today make Basin Bayou's relatively open character a non-issue through mid-morning — an ideal window to pole or drift the interior grass flats sight-fishing for reds on the falling tide. The outgoing tide pulling toward the 4:20 PM low will start moving fish off the flats and toward the bayou mouth through mid-morning, so begin shallow and work your way out as water drops. Slightly stained water limits visibility for sight-fishing but a push poling approach with weedless soft plastics or a slow-rolled shrimp imitation will still find fish in the grass. Get off the water before 1 PM; this spot's limited protection means you don't want to be caught here if afternoon storms materialize.

lagrange.aiNote: LaGrange Bayou is the top trout producer among the bayous on this dashboard, with legendary oyster bars at the mouth and interior grass flats that hold redfish year-round. Deep interior holes are reliable for black drum and sheepshead, and the bayou offers the most protected water on this side of the bay — the go-to spot when weather threatens. It draws more pressure than Basin Bayou but produces consistently across seasons.
lagrange.todaysCall: This is a high-percentage stop today: the falling tide after a spring-tide high will flush bait hard across the oyster bar mouths right through the prime morning window, setting up a textbook trout-and-redfish ambush. Late June reports had trout and redfish both active across Choctawhatchee Bay, and LaGrange's oyster bars are exactly the structure those fish gravitate to when tides are moving. Fish the bar edges and drop-offs first with a popping cork and live shrimp or a soft plastic on a light jig head; as the tide drops further, probe the deeper interior holes for black drum and sheepshead. Slightly stained water and a new moon (low ambient light even at dawn) both favor earlier, more aggressive presentations — be on the water at or before first light. LaGrange's protection makes it a viable option even if clouds build later, but still aim to wrap by 1 PM.

fourmile.aiNote: Four Mile Creek is a short tidal creek running between Shipyard Marina and the bay, where tidal flow pushes baitfish up the creek on incoming tides and concentrates redfish and trout in the bends and grass edges. The creek mouth is a prime flounder zone, and the upper section transitions toward brackish water with bass and smaller reds mixed in. Its compact, sheltered layout makes it the safest fishery on this dashboard when weather threatens.
fourmile.todaysCall: The tide is falling all morning toward a 4:20 PM low, which means baitfish will be flushing back out through the creek — work the bends and grass edges near mid-creek first, then move toward the mouth as water drops and fish stage before exiting into the bay. The creek mouth flounder zone is worth a few casts as the outgoing tide concentrates mullet and small pinfish in the shallower slots; slow-dragged paddle tails or gulp shrimp on the bottom are the play. With today's light west winds and protected layout, comfort won't be an issue through the morning, but the summer heat index of 103°F means shade is scarce inside the creek — stay hydrated and fish efficiently. If afternoon storms materialize after 1 PM, Four Mile Creek is your best bail-out option on this dashboard.

hogtown.aiNote: Hogtown Bayou is a signature Santa Rosa Beach guide spot and one of the most productive trout flats on Choctawhatchee Bay, with fish stacked on grass in two to four feet of water during summer mornings. Spanish mackerel show at the mouth on moving tides, and the location draws regular pressure but produces consistently throughout the season. Factor in the longer run time from the 331 Bridge compared to the bayous on the Freeport side.
hogtown.todaysCall: This is the spot most directly supported by the late June bite reports, which called out quality trout near Santa Rosa Beach — Hogtown Bayou is the textbook address for that pattern, and conditions today are favorable if you get there early. Plan for the longer run and be on the grass flats as close to first light as possible; summer trout here are most active before the sun beats down, and the falling tide through mid-morning will keep bait moving across the flat. Topwaters and weedless soft plastics worked over the two-to-four-foot grass are the classic morning approach; switch to a slower subsurface presentation as the sun climbs. Keep an eye on the mouth for Spanish mackerel on any tide movement, and build extra buffer time into your return trip given the run distance and the post-1 PM storm window.

mallet.aiNote: Mallet Bayou is a small tributary that feeds directly into LaGrange Bayou just south of Freeport, and its direct connection to one of the bay's top trout-and-redfish producers means LaGrange's oyster-bar patterns plausibly extend into this quieter, less-pressured water. There is significantly less documented fishing history for Mallet Bayou itself, so confidence is lower than for its larger neighbor. Its small, interior character makes it a natural calm-water fallback when wind or weather pushes anglers off the open bay.
mallet.todaysCall: Today's light winds and modest storm risk make this a reasonable exploratory option for anglers who want to avoid LaGrange's heavier pressure while staying on the same productive water system. Work the connection point between Mallet and LaGrange on the falling tide — any bait flushing out of Mallet will draw reds and trout to that junction. Slightly stained water is no handicap in tight, shallow water like this; go with a weedless soft plastic or weightless live shrimp and work the banks slowly. Manage expectations relative to LaGrange — this is a lower-confidence, potentially rewarding side trip, not a proven primary destination.

mack.aiNote: Mack Bayou sits on the barrier-island, 30-A side of Choctawhatchee Bay near Topsail Hill Preserve State Park — a long run from the 331 Bridge that should be treated as a destination trip, not a quick local stop. It shares the same protected-bayou character as Alaqua and LaGrange, with marsh grass, oyster bars, and interior holes, and sees less pressure simply because of the distance involved. Hewett Bayou and Buck Bayou sit immediately to the east and are realistically fishable in the same trip.
mack.todaysCall: If you're willing to make the run, today's light west winds and calm morning conditions are about as good as it gets for the long haul to the 30-A bayous — but leave the dock well before sunrise to maximize your fishable window before heat and the post-1 PM storm chance shrink it. Fish the oyster bars and marsh grass edges at the mouth on the falling tide, targeting redfish and trout with the same early-morning approach that works across the bay. Slightly stained water is consistent with what you'll find elsewhere today — expect normal presentations to hold. Budget time to also hit Hewett and potentially Buck Bayou on the same trip; making the run for just one small bayou is rarely the most efficient use of the day.

hewett.aiNote: Hewett Bayou sits immediately east of Mack Bayou on the barrier-island, 30-A side of Choctawhatchee Bay near Topsail Hill Preserve State Park, sharing the same protected-bayou habitat of oyster bars, marsh grass, and deeper interior holes. Like Mack Bayou, it's a long run from the 331 Bridge and sees light pressure as a result. It pairs naturally with Mack and Buck Bayou in a single trip.
hewett.todaysCall: The same logic that applies to Mack Bayou today applies here — light west winds and calm morning conditions justify the long run if you plan the trip correctly and depart early. Hit the mouth structure on the falling tide first, working oyster bar edges for trout and reds before moving deeper into the interior holes as water drops. Light pressure at this distance from the main ramps means fish here are less wary than at closer spots; the slightly stained water is a neutral factor, so standard soft plastics and shrimp presentations should produce. Pair with Mack and Buck Bayou and be pointed toward home well before 1 PM given the storm window and the run time back.

buck.aiNote: Buck Bayou is the smallest and least-documented of the three neighboring bayous on the barrier-island, 30-A side of Choctawhatchee Bay near Topsail Hill Preserve State Park. Its habitat should track its larger neighbors — marsh grass, some oyster structure, and a modest interior — but there is less basis to speak confidently about its specific fishing character. It is best approached as a bonus stop on a Mack and Hewett Bayou trip rather than a standalone destination.
buck.todaysCall: Buck Bayou makes most sense today as a quick exploratory add-on after fishing Mack and Hewett — if the tide and time allow, poke in and work the mouth structure on the falling tide for opportunistic reds and trout. Don't burn your prime early-morning window here; prioritize Mack and Hewett first and treat Buck as a low-pressure bonus cast on the way back. Expectations should be calibrated accordingly — this is the thinnest confidence play on the dashboard, and today is not the day to gamble a long run on a single unknown small bayou. If Mack and Hewett are producing, stay there rather than rushing to cover Buck before the storm window opens.
